excerpt: Cheyenne contract cleaning costs run about 9% below national benchmarks, but high plains wind and government-adjacent security add real labor. Office managers get a three-times-weekly cost index for 2,000 to 25,000 sq ft, district notes, and a Wyoming vetting checklist.
quickAnswer: Cheyenne, WY offices typically pay $0.104–$0.173 per sq ft per visit under 2,500 sq ft and $0.043–$0.086 per sq ft per visit for buildings above 25,000 sq ft once the 0.91x city multiplier and a 3x-weekly schedule are applied. A 10,000 sq ft Dell Range office cleaned three times a week usually budgets $7,867–$13,486 per month, and hourly specialty work runs $32–$55.

blocks.text: The Cheyenne Cleaning Cost Index at a Glance

Cheyenne's office market is shaped by state government, F.E. Warren Air Force Base contractors, rail and logistics firms, and a growing cluster of data-center and back-office operations. That mix creates steady demand for after-hours janitorial service but a relatively small pool of established commercial vendors. With a janitor median wage reference around $15.02 per hour, local pricing settles at about 0.91x the national benchmark.

Many Cheyenne tenants, especially in government-adjacent suites and medical offices, run three cleanings per week: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday nights. At 13 visits per month and a 0.95 frequency multiplier, that schedule balances appearance against cost better than daily service for offices under 50 occupants. The index below uses that cadence on a carpet baseline.

blocks.title: Reading the index
blocks.text: A 5,000 sq ft suite at $0.09 national equals $450 per visit. Apply the 0.95 three-times-weekly multiplier ($427.50) and the 0.91 Cheyenne multiplier to reach about $389 per visit, then multiply by 13 visits for roughly $5,057 per month. Drop to twice weekly and the per-visit figure rises to about $410, but monthly spend falls to around $3,546.
Downtown Capitol, Dell Range, and Business Parkway Profiles

Downtown Capitol offices around the Wyoming State Capitol, Capitol Avenue, and the historic depot area include state agency annexes, law firms, lobbying offices, and associations. Older buildings mean terrazzo, ceramic restrooms, radiators, and tall window sills that collect dust. Security protocols and key control push bids toward the upper half of the range.

The Dell Range Boulevard corridor is Cheyenne's main suburban office and retail spine, with medical practices, insurance agencies, banks, and franchise headquarters in newer single-story buildings. Easy parking and open floor plans make it the most cost-efficient district to clean, though heavy foot traffic from surface lots means entry floors get punished. Business Parkway and the nearby industrial-office parks host logistics, engineering, and data-center support offices where crews may clean office wings attached to warehouse or technical space with different flooring and access rules.

items: Downtown Capitol: older finishes and badge or escort requirements typically land at the upper end of the index.
Dell Range: lowest effective rates; prioritize entry matting and LVT damp mopping every visit.
Business Parkway: confirm which zones are in scope, since office wings may adjoin warehouses with sealed concrete at a 0.95 flooring multiplier.
Base-adjacent contractor suites: expect background-check lead times that delay a contract start by one to three weeks.

blocks.text: High Plains Wind Dust and Winter Snow Tracking

Cheyenne is one of the windiest cities in the United States, and sustained gusts drive fine dust through door sweeps, window frames, and rooftop air handlers. Interior glass, monitor screens, and horizontal surfaces near exterior walls dull quickly. In winter, snow and magnesium chloride from parking lots get tracked straight onto lobby floors, leaving a white film that is slippery when wet and abrasive when dry.

Equipment choices make that manageable. A 3x12 ft corrugated rubber runner, such as the Rubber-Cal ribbed runner at 1/8-inch thickness, gives service and side entries a non-slip, hose-cleanable surface that traps slush before it spreads. At reception and security desks where staff stand for hours, a 5/8-inch closed-cell Wearwell 24/7 anti-fatigue mat with beveled edges resists deicer chemicals and keeps a trip hazard from forming. Crews using a HYGEN 18-inch microfiber flat mop kit with an onboard reservoir can pass over entry LVT every visit without hauling a bucket, which removes chloride film in minutes rather than redistributing it.

blocks.title: Do not let deicer film build up
blocks.text: Magnesium and calcium chloride residue left on floor finish softens it and causes a hazy white bloom. If your vendor only dust-mops entries in winter, the finish will need a full strip and recoat by spring, a project that can cost more than a whole season of daily damp mopping.

Wyoming runs a monopolistic state workers' compensation fund, so private carriers cannot write coverage for most employers. That makes verification straightforward: ask the vendor for its Wyoming Workers' Compensation certificate and confirm the account is active. A general liability certificate from a private carrier does not substitute for state workers' comp coverage.

items.name: Verify state workers' comp
items.text: Request the Wyoming Department of Workforce Services certificate and confirm it covers janitorial classifications, not just office staff.

items.name: Check liability limits
items.text: Require at least $1 million per occurrence general liability and name the tenant and building owner as additional insureds on the COI.

items.name: Clarify screening
items.text: For state, federal-contractor, or base-adjacent suites, specify the background-check standard, who pays for it, and how replacement staff are cleared.

items.name: Confirm OSHA programs
items.text: Ask for the HazCom written program, SDS sheets for every chemical brought on site, and bloodborne pathogens training for restroom crews.

items.name: Define key control
items.text: Document key and badge issuance, alarm codes, and the procedure if a cleaner leaves the company mid-contract.

blocks.text: At the 0.91x multiplier, restroom service benchmarks translate to about $13.65–$27.30 per restroom per visit, breakroom sanitation to roughly $10.92–$22.75, and interior glass to $13.65–$31.85. Quarterly deep floor care amortizes to about $0.027–$0.055 per sq ft per month, or $273–$546 monthly for a 10,000 sq ft office. Given the wind, interior glass and high dusting deliver the most visible improvement per dollar.

faqs.q: Is three-times-weekly cleaning enough for a Cheyenne office?
faqs.a: For most offices under about 50 people with one or two restrooms, yes. Three visits per month per week equals 13 visits monthly at 4.33 weeks per month. Busy clinics, offices with public counters, or buildings with heavy winter entry traffic may still need daily restroom and entry service, often handled as a short day-porter add-on.

faqs.q: How does Wyoming workers' compensation differ from other states?
faqs.a: Wyoming operates a state-run monopolistic fund, so coverage comes through the state rather than private insurers. Ask the vendor for its state certificate, confirm the account is active, and do not accept a private general liability policy as a substitute. Uncovered workers injured on site can create liability exposure for you.

faqs.q: What does government-adjacent screening add to the price?
faqs.a: Background checks, fingerprinting, and escort requirements add administrative time and limit which cleaners can be scheduled. Vendors usually recover that through a modest per-visit premium or a one-time onboarding fee. Ask for it as a separate line so you can see the cost of security rather than having it buried in the sq ft rate.

faqs.q: Which cleaning tasks are usually excluded from Cheyenne contracts?
faqs.a: Exterior window washing, snow removal, carpet extraction, high dusting above about 10 feet, and floor strip-and-wax projects are commonly excluded or billed separately. Make sure the proposal lists exclusions explicitly and gives unit pricing for each so you can approve extra work without renegotiating.

faqs.q: Should Cheyenne offices require green-certified cleaning chemicals?
faqs.a: Green Seal or EPA Safer Choice products are a sensible default in enclosed, low-humidity offices where dust and fragrances circulate. For restrooms and high-touch surfaces, still require EPA-registered disinfectants and confirm crews follow the labeled dwell time so the product actually works.
